answers.core:
This proposal is specifically about improving the **built-in FileSystem dock’s usability**:

- The FileSystem dock is a central part of the editor workflow, used by all projects, and its “Filter Files” field is already the natural place where users expect to type search terms.
- Adding a simple AND/OR expression syntax directly there keeps the experience **consistent and discoverable**, instead of forcing users to rely on a separate custom dock or asset.
- The change is small, self-contained, and backward compatible: users who never need AND/OR logic can keep using the filter exactly as before.
- Having this in core benefits all users out of the box, without requiring them to search the asset library, install, and maintain extra plugins just to get basic multi-keyword filtering.

Because of this, it feels like a natural, core usability improvement rather than something that should live only as an optional add-on.
answers.workaround:
It can be partially worked around with an editor plugin, but not in a convenient or fully integrated way:

- A plugin can create its own dock with a custom search box and a list of results, implementing `&` / `|` logic in GDScript.
- However, this means users have to **use an additional panel** instead of the built-in FileSystem dock they already rely on.
- A plugin cannot easily replace or intercept the internal filtering logic of the existing FileSystem dock, so behavior becomes fragmented:
  - The built-in “Filter Files” field still behaves as a simple substring filter.
  - The plugin panel behaves differently, which can be confusing and inconsistent.

So while a plugin can approximate the feature, it is not particularly convenient and does not improve the default out-of-the-box experience of the FileSystem dock.

title: Allow simple AND/OR expressions in the “Filter Files” field of the FileSystem dock
